description: CSS-OS is the optical survey of the China Space Station Telescope. Cao et al. (2018) define seven photometric bands, NUV, u, g, r, i, z and y, and show intrinsic filter transmission separately from total transmission that includes detector quantum efficiency. Gong et al. (2025) describe the survey camera as those seven bands plus slitless bands GU, GV and GI.
facility_description: The China Space Station Telescope is an off-axis three-mirror anastigmat with a 2 m primary mirror, scheduled to launch in 2027 and to co-orbit with the China Space Station.
notes: No CSST or NAOC data-policy page was opened. https://www.nao.cas.cn/csst/mission/overview/ did not return (curl HTTP 000). The Meng PDF https://www.issibern.ch/teams/weakgravlense/wp-content/uploads/2019/11/X.M.-Meng.pdf returned HTTP 500. Both arXiv records (1706.09586 and 2507.04618) link only to the arXiv non-exclusive distribution licence, which is a grant by the submitter to arXiv.org, not a grant to redistribute numerical curves. Journal HTML for MNRAS was not opened. NJM names ending _fil and _ccd, and wNUV, wg and wi, are not used as filenames or band names on the pages opened. Cao et al. (2018) Figure 1 separates intrinsic transmission from total transmission including detector quantum efficiency. Cao et al. (2022) Figure 1, for the survey-camera filters, says the dotted curves are detector quantum efficiency, the dashed lines intrinsic transmission, and the solid lines total transmission including quantum efficiency. Those captions do not name _fil or _ccd files, so no component band is described here. Gong et al. (2025) Table 1 prints GI with an asterisk; the extracted text has no footnote for it. Author funding acknowledgements in Gong et al. are not a requested user citation, so acknowledgements is omitted. The numerical curves, if taken from these papers, do not have an owner statement that clearly allows redistribution.

NUV.Description: CSS-OS photometric band NUV. Cao et al. (2018) Table 1 lists mean wavelength 2877 Å, FWHM 701 Å and top transmission 65%.

GU.Description: CSST survey-camera slitless spectroscopic band GU. Gong et al. (2025) Table 1 lists 255-410 nm.

GV.Description: CSST survey-camera slitless spectroscopic band GV. Gong et al. (2025) Table 1 lists 400-640 nm.

GI.Description: CSST survey-camera slitless spectroscopic band GI. Gong et al. (2025) Table 1 lists 620-1000 nm. The table prints GI with an asterisk; the extracted text has no footnote for that asterisk.
